response.sql: SELECT translink, ordertypedist, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER (PARTITION BY ordertypedist) AS fraction FROM (SELECT a.translink AS translink, t.ordertypedist AS ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON t.transreg = a.translink WHERE a.peercorr > 0.149 AND t.ordertypedist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a.translink, t.ordertypedist) ORDER BY fraction DESC, translink, ordertypedist LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: 'High peer correlation' means peercorr strictly greater than 0.149 (the cutoff itself is excluded).

The count is the number of matched (advancedbehavior, transactionrecord) joined rows per translink and ordertypedist. The denominator is the sum of those counts across all translinks sharing the same ordertypedist, after the peercorr filter and the removal of missing order type mixes.
Ties in the fraction are broken by translink, then ordertypedist, so the top 10 is deterministic.

alternatives.interpretation: High peer correlation is inclusive of the cutoff (peercorr >= 0.149).
